passages.original: tamen necessarium est damnatae praevaricationis divinum quoque praesens proferre documentum : et sicut in Ario impia secta ejus, divina animadversione punita, praejudicat et de sectatoribus ejus, quod eadem illos poena maneat qua torquetur et Arius : ita de praevaricatoribus poe- nis praesentibus divino judicio determinatum est.
passages.english: Nevertheless it is necessary to bring forward also a present divine proof concerning the condemned betrayal [of the faith]: and just as in the case of Arius his impious sect, punished by divine chastisement, gives a prior judgement also concerning his followers, that the same penalty awaits them by which Arius too is tormented, so concerning the betrayers it has been determined by divine judgement through present penalties.
passages.notes: 'praevaricatio' / 'praevaricatores' refers to those who lapsed or betrayed the faith, presumably those who yielded to Arian pressure, as opposed to those who held firm. The construction 'in Ario impia secta ejus ... praejudicat' is loose; it is rendered as 'in the case of Arius his impious sect ... gives a prior judgement'. 'poe- nis' is a line-break split for 'poenis'.

passages.original: Quos quidem libros, cum per omnia ex integro ageret, suspexit et Atha- nasius, ut veri vindices, atque in Graecum stylum transtulit, ne tantum boni Graeca lingua non habe- ret. Parum est, quin etiam propriis litteris idem Athanasius eosdem libros praedicat, ut Prophetarum et Evangelistarum atque Apostolorum doctrinis et pia confessione contextos. Et quamvis plurimis in cum laudibus erigatur, tamen non aequat ad meriti ejus praeconium, et quidem cum amplios laudare non posset : 1 ita rerum supereminentia quaevis lau- dans lingua superatur.
passages.english: These books, since he [Lucifer] dealt with everything in them in its entirety, Athanasius too admired as [the work of] a champion of the truth, and translated them into Greek, so that the Greek language should not lack so great a good. Nor is that all: the same Athanasius also, in letters of his own, commends these same books as woven together from the teachings of the Prophets, Evangelists and Apostles and from a pious confession. And although he rises to very many praises of him, yet he does not come up to the proclamation his merit deserves, and indeed since he could not praise him more fully: so does the surpassing greatness of the subject overcome any tongue that praises [it].
passages.notes: The author of the books addressed to Constantius is not named in the passage or context; the books to Constantius are presumably those of Lucifer of Cagliari (this libellus is by the Luciferian presbyters Faustinus and Marcellinus), not Hilary. The subject is only implied. 'in cum' read as 'in eum' (scanning error). 'amplios' read as 'amplius'. 'ut veri vindices' taken as 'as [books of] a champion of truth'; the plural 'vindices' is awkward and may be corrupt. The stray '1' is a footnote mark. The final sentence is loosely constructed and its sense is somewhat uncertain.
